summary: Regional latency spike causing request timeouts - suspected cross-region routing
description:
Issue summary:
- Customer (AtlasHealth, dedicated) reports increased inference latency and intermittent request timeouts starting ~2026-03-02 12:20 UTC. Errors seen are request timeouts (client-side) and 502/504 from the gateway in some traces. Suspected cross-region routing or regional networking degradation.

Impact:
- A subset of requests from AtlasHealth are timing out or experiencing 3-6s delay spikes. Customer has critical workflow with synchronous calls to Redwood; impact is user-visible and causing failed transactions. Estimated 8-12% of requests from us-east are affected during peak.

Environment:
- prod/us-east primary, some traffic routed to fallbacks in eu-west. Affected models: redwood-rlhf-1.1 (default), gpt-like-open-2.7b (fallback).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send synchronous chat completion request to customer route (route id available in logs).
2) Repeat under moderate QPS (5-10 r/s).
3) Observe that ~1 in 10 requests either take >2s or hit client timeout at 10s.

Observed logs / metrics referenced:
- Gateway traces show increased upstream latency for serving-runtime instances in us-east-1a between 12:18-13:05 UTC.
- Routing service logs show several route decisions selecting eu-west model variants for us-east-origin requests during the window.
- Netflow and BGP alerts from provider show transient packet loss and AS path changes impacting us-east->eu-west routes.

Customer timeline:
- 2026-03-02 12:22 UTC: Customer sends first alert to support via support portal.
- 2026-03-02 12:35 UTC: Support acknowledged and started triage.
- 2026-03-02 12:50 UTC: Engineering looped in (INT-8123).
comments: 2026-03-02 12:36 UTC - Sofia Martinez (Support): Acknowledged. Collecting traces and asking for request IDs. Requested customer logs and sample request timestamps.

2026-03-02 12:52 UTC - Aaron Patel (SRE): Noted routing anomalies in logs. Observed policy-based routing fallback to eu-west for some us-east requests between 12:18-12:55 UTC. Investigating whether autoscaler or capacity drain caused cross-region fallback.
2026-03-02 13:10 UTC - Customer (AtlasHealth): Provided sample request IDs and traces. Reports retries temporarily helped but intermittent failures persist.

2026-03-02 14:05 UTC - Aaron Patel (SRE): Confirmed upstream packet loss reported by cloud provider during window. We temporarily adjusted routing policy to prefer local healthy endpoints; started mitigation for ongoing traffic.

2026-03-03 09:30 UTC - Priya Desai (Eng - Serving Runtime): Deployed a conservative routing policy change to reduce cross-region fallbacks during transient capacity signals. Monitoring for regressions.
2026-03-04 11:00 UTC - Sofia Martinez (Support): Customer confirmed reduction in timeouts after routing adjustment. Monitoring continues; pending full postmortem and permanent fix.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Regional network provider experienced transient packet loss/BGP changes leading to increased RTT and packet drops; routing policy triggered cross-region fallbacks for perceived unhealthy local endpoints.
Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler or maintenance triggered short-lived instance drains in us-east AZ, combined with conservative local health check thresholds caused traffic shift to eu-west variants.

Checks performed:
- Collected gateway traces and correlated with serving-runtime latency metrics and host-level metrics.
- Queried routing decision logs for affected request IDs; found 12:18-12:55 UTC window where policy chose eu-west backends for ~9% of us-east-origin requests.
- Looked at cloud provider status and BGP/Netflow exports; found provider-reported packet loss in the path between us-east rack clusters and edge.

Partial findings:
- Cloud provider reported and mitigated an upstream network event at 12:40 UTC; event duration aligns with customer impact window.
- Routing policy currently uses a combination of healthy-check score and latency thresholds; the health-check scoring appears to be overly sensitive to short-lived latency spikes, which increased cross-region routing.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Adjusted routing policy to weight local healthy score higher and increased sensitivity window to avoid immediate cross-region fallback on sub-minute spikes. This reduced client-observed timeouts for the customer.
resolution_notes: Workaround: Routing policy tweaked to prefer in-region backends during short-lived latency anomalies; customer pinned route to us-east model variant as immediate mitigation.

Permanent fix plan: 1) Update routing policy to include a decay window and hysteresis for health checks; 2) Add automated detection for provider-level network events to avoid automated cross-region failover; 3) Add runbook steps for faster rollback of routing policy.
Rollout notes: Conservative policy update deployed 2026-03-03 09:25 UTC to canaries, then to global traffic. Monitoring shows restored p95 latency for affected customer routes.
Customer communication: Informed AtlasHealth of mitigation and next steps; offered 10% credit for the impacted billing period and scheduled postmortem call for 2026-03-05.
Ticket status: Monitoring - change to Resolved once postmortem published and policy PR merged (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1456).
follow_up_tasks: INT-8123: Investigate autoscaler signals and instance drain behavior during provider network events
Create automated alert for cross-region latency anomalies and sudden rise in cross-region routing decisions
Postmortem and RCA to be published to Confluence by 2026-03-06
Improve routing policy tests to simulate provider-level packet loss and ensure hysteresis behaves as expected
